newsitem.title: USA: "I want my MBS" - FNMA celebrates 15 years.
newsitem.headline: "I want my MBS" - FNMA celebrates 15 years.

text.p: The Federal National Mortgage Association touted the 15th anniversary of its mortgaged-backed securities (MBS) on Friday, drawing comparisons with another 15-year-old phenomenon: MTV.
Mortgage-backed securities, Fannie Mae suggested, have brought fresh money into the U.S. mortgage market just as MTV has brought fresh music to the public.
The securities have also helped Americans save money when buying homes, by bringing mortgage rates lower in relation to other interest rates, Fannie Mae pointed out.

"The $1.3 trillion in Fannie Mae MBS issued in 15 years represents the enormous success of this vital way to fund mortgages in the U.S., one that attracts money from all over the world into the American mortgage market," Robert Levin, executive vice president at Fannie Mae, said Friday.
The annual issuance of Fannie Mae MBS has grown from $717 million in 1981 to a peak of $221 billion in 1993, Levin said at a press breakfast Friday..
"With $129 billion issued between January and October, 1996 is poised to become the strongest year for Fannie Mae MBS issues since 1993," he said.
While the annual issuance of Fannie Mae MBS issuance has grown over the past 15 years, the spreads over Treasuries, a benchmark comparison, have narrowed substantially, he said.

For example, Levin said the average spread between 30-year mortgage commitment rates and 10-year Treasuries in 1981 was 273 basis points. In 1996, the spread has averaged 137 basis points for the first three quarters of the year, half the level of 1981.
The narrowing of Fannie Mae yield spreads over Treasuries is indicative of a highly liquid secondary mortgage-backed market with a daily trading volume in the tens of billions of dollars, said Levin.
Looking forward, Levin said Fannie Mae will continue to construct new products and tap into new technologies in order to generate greater capital market flexibility and liquidity.
